item.title: Dude In A Crazy Fit Inspires Memes About How To Spot A Filipino
item.description: How Did You Know I'm Filipino is a series of memes, including video edits and AI-generated edits based on an edited image of a Filipino man wearing a flared, baggy jeans, big shoes and a black hoodie, sometimes referred to as an "hourglass fit" for its shape. In December 2025, the image became the subject of memes which suggest that the outfit is a telltale sign that the person is Filipino. The image is often further edited in absurd ways as part of the meme. As the meme went viral, TikToker @hu

item.title: Graph Ranking Well Written Anime Characters Goes Viral, Sparking Discourse And Edits
item.description: Main Characters How Well Written They Are is an exploitable meme format showing a graph of main characters from a variety of anime series, meant to rank how well written they are. The original graph, posted by X / Twitter user @rezeistweeting in late December 2025, ranks One Piece protagonist Monkey D. Luffy as the best written in comparison to characters like Naruto, Goku, Ichigo and more. The post inspired discourse and edits that replace the original characters with other characters.

item.title: Epstein Has Become The Focus Of Countless Viral Fancam Edits In Bizarre Shortform Video Trend
item.description: Jeffrey Epstein Edits refers to fancam-style, often AI-assisted video edits revolving around and often ironically glazing up deceased sex trafficker Jeffrey Epstein. Epstein edits began appearing online as early as January 2024 and saw a boost in virality in December 2025 surrounding the release of the redacted Epstein files. Some of the edits are set to slowed down or otherwise remixed versions of "Boss" by Lil Pump and the "EFN" song.

item.title: On This Day 13 Years Ago, The 'Why Are You Booing Me? I'm Right' Meme Appeared On 'The Eric Andre Show'
item.description: Why Are You Booing Me? I’m Right refers to a reaction image taken from The Eric Andre Show of comedian Hannibal Burress addressing a crowd with the phrase “Why are you booing me? I’m right!” The image began being used with unpopular truths several years after the episode aired.

item.title: To Celebrate The New Year, You Can Once Again Become A New You
item.description: New Year, New Me refers to a catchphrase used to caption memes made before and after New Year's Eve and New Year's Day. The phrase infers that the person will change after New Year's, likely in accordance with their New Year's resolution. However, the phrase is most often used ironically by portraying no intention to change. item.title: Ring In The New Year With The Classic Moment Of Ninja's Times Square Floss Fail
item.description: Ninja's Times Square Floss Fail refers to a failed attempt by Mixer streamer Tyler "Ninja" Blevins to get attendees of the Times Square New Year's Eve celebration in New York to perform the floss dance.

item.title: Was Your New Year's Eve As Lit As The One They Had In Manchester Back In 2016?
item.description: The Manchester New Year’s Photo is a photoshop meme based on a photograph taken during 2016 New Year’s Eve revelry in Manchester, England.
